# Security Audit Evidence

Last updated: 2026-06-01

Scope: SEC-AUTH, SEC-EDGE, SEC-IAP, SEC-RLS, SEC-MTLS, SEC-REWARD, SEC-PII, SEC-AIT

## Current Verdict

Local code and regression evidence is in place for the requested security audit. Supabase management access for the current project has been restored by making the live audit helper prefer the project credentials pinned in `.mcp.json`, so a stale shell `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` can no longer point the audit at the wrong project.

Latest live management checks on 2026-06-01:

```bash
supabase functions list --project-ref gxvtgrcqkbdibkyeqyil
supabase migration list --linked --output json
supabase secrets list --project-ref gxvtgrcqkbdibkyeqyil
```

Latest observed result on 2026-06-02: function `verify_jwt` settings PASS for 6 protected functions, linked security migrations PASS `17/17`, and required Edge secret names PASS. `OPENAI_API_KEY` was restored from the backend environment into Supabase Edge secrets on 2026-06-01, and `generate-report` was redeployed to `ACTIVE version=5` with `verify_jwt=true`.

Do not mark the full security goal complete until live Edge logs are scanned and authenticated RLS cross-access fixtures are verified.

As of 2026-06-01, the full `npm run security:live-audit` helper no longer stops at the first management issue. It records the local AIT upload artifact scan first, verifies live function settings and linked migrations when credentials are available, checks required Edge secret names, requires a live Edge log export for the PII scan, requires authenticated RLS cross-access fixtures, continues through public Edge/Backend spoof probes, and exits non-zero at the end while preserving all reachable runtime evidence.

## Latest Live Edge Spoof Probe

`npm run security:live-audit` and `npm run security:live-audit -- --edge-probes-only` run public Edge probes with the public anon key against Edge URLs. Latest full-audit public probe result on 2026-06-01 after the Supabase settings restore and `generate-report` redeploy:

Auth-code probe: `login-with-toss` is called with `authorizationCode=security-probe-expired-or-reused-auth-code`, `referrer=SANDBOX`, and a valid nonce, once normally and once with `x-user-role: trainer`. Latest public probe result: `502 / 502`, spoof request id `019e82a1-b4e1-774e-bb11-20d7048bd26d`, PASS. The expected result is that both calls fail and no Supabase session is issued. Local tests still carry the stronger replay proof for a previously consumed successful code; this public live probe proves the deployed auth bridge does not accept an invalid/expired-style code or role-spoofed variant. The response body was also scanned for auth-code/token/PII echoes and passed.

| Function | Anon / spoof status | Malformed JWT / spoof status | Expired-test JWT / spoof status | Spoof request id | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verify-iap-order` | 401 / 401 | 401 / 401 | 401 / 401 | `019e82a1-bbe3-7c88-a5c6-07b9566b9654` | PASS |
| `grant-toss-points` | 403 / 403 | 401 / 401 | 401 / 401 | `019e82a1-c043-718f-bc9b-ec7e1929a31c` | PASS |
| `send-smart-message` | 403 / 403 | 401 / 401 | 401 / 401 | `019e82a1-c3e4-78b6-b930-9321fbff586f` | PASS |
| `generate-report` | 403 / 403 | 401 / 401 | 401 / 401 | `019e82a1-c754-7a9b-a191-2babc60975a7` | PASS |

Interpretation: the spoofed role header did not turn any anonymous, malformed-JWT, or expired-test-JWT probe into a successful privileged call, and failure response bodies did not echo probe auth codes, JWTs, service keys, Toss user keys, phone numbers, or emails. Management-level verification now confirms live function `verify_jwt` settings and linked migrations; live log export is still required for the final log PII scan.

The `generate-report` probe includes `report_date`, so it exercises the auth/report-scope path instead of stopping at the missing-parameter branch.

Interpretation: public FastAPI protected routes reject anonymous access, malformed JWTs, expired-test JWTs, and `x-user-role: trainer` spoof attempts before returning user, subscription, dashboard, dog, or usage data, and before accepting dog creation, quick logs, coaching job creation, settings updates, IAP proxy calls, or B2B report creation. The failure response bodies were also scanned for auth-code/token/PII echoes and passed. The full command still exits non-zero at the end with two explicit blockers: missing live Edge log export and missing authenticated RLS attacker JWT/fixture inputs. This does not replace authenticated cross-user and cross-org tests, which remain covered locally and still require live RLS/project verification after real attacker/victim fixtures are available.

## Authenticated RLS Cross-Access Probe

`npm run security:live-audit -- --rls-probes-only` now supports live cross-user checks that do not require Supabase management privileges. Complete proof requires a real attacker user JWT plus the full fixture set below, all belonging to a different owner/org:

```bash
SECURITY_RLS_ATTACKER_JWT=<attacker-user-access-token> \
npm run security:live-audit -- --rls-probes-only \
  --rls-dog-id <other-users-dog-id> \
  --rls-coaching-id <other-users-coaching-id> \
  --rls-generation-job-id <other-users-coaching-generation-job-id> \
  --rls-subscription-user-id <other-user-id> \
  --rls-toss-order-id <other-users-toss-order-row-id> \
  --rls-org-id <other-org-id> \
  --rls-report-id <other-report-id>
```

By default the helper now fails if any required RLS resource id is missing, so a partial fixture cannot be mistaken for full SEC-RLS proof. Use `--rls-allow-partial` only for an explicitly scoped diagnostic run. Full `npm run security:live-audit` now runs the same authenticated RLS cross-access probes automatically; `--rls-probes-only` remains available for focused diagnostics. The probe checks Supabase REST RLS directly for `dogs`, `dog_env`, `behavior_logs`, `training_step_attempts`, `case_intakes`, `user_training_status`, `training_behavior_snapshots`, `ai_recommendation_snapshots`, `ai_recommendation_feedback`, `ai_coaching`, `action_tracker`, `coaching_generation_jobs`, `subscriptions`, `user_entitlements`, `user_settings`, `toss_orders`, `organizations`, `org_members`, `org_dogs`, `dog_assignments`, `org_subscriptions`, `media_assets`, and `daily_reports`; any returned row is treated as a read leak. It also runs `PATCH {}` with `Prefer: return=representation` against those same targets, so any returned row is treated as an update-policy leak without intentionally changing row values. It now also runs forged insert probes for sensitive write surfaces: `case_intakes`, `user_training_status`, `ai_recommendation_snapshots`, `action_tracker`, `coaching_generation_jobs`, `subscriptions`, `user_entitlements`, `user_settings`, `toss_orders`, `organizations`, `org_members`, `org_subscriptions`, `org_dogs`, `dog_assignments`, `media_assets`, and `daily_reports`. Any 2xx insert response is treated as a privilege leak, while RLS/schema/FK rejection responses remain acceptable. Finally, it calls FastAPI resource routes for the same dog/org/report ids and fails on any 2xx response. The FastAPI side now covers both reads and authenticated attacker mutations: dog profile `PUT`, quick log creation, coaching generation job creation, training status upsert, org update, member invite, org dog enrollment, dog assignment, report creation, report update, and report send. Latest 2026-06-01 run without a JWT correctly fails closed at input validation: `Missing --rls-attacker-jwt or SECURITY_RLS_ATTACKER_JWT for --probe-rls`. Live cross-user read/write proof remains pending until real test JWT/resource-id pairs are available.

Latest local regression set used for the audit:

```bash
Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py Backend/tests/test_security.py Backend/tests/test_log_redaction.py Backend/tests/test_org_security.py Backend/tests/test_coaching_security.py Backend/tests/test_report_service.py Backend/tests/test_referral_security.py Backend/tests/test_subscription_security.py Backend/tests/test_subscription_entitlements.py -q
```

Generate Report scope evidence: `generate-report` now resolves the `daily_reports` row before AI generation, requires the requested `dog_id` to match that row, and treats `created_by_org_id` as the authoritative scope whenever it is present. A trainer id match alone is no longer enough for an org-created report; the handler must find an active `org_members` row with one of the standard B2B roles. Latest focused validation: `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='generate-report'` passed 21 suites / 162 tests, and `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_generate_report_binds_requested_dog_to_report_row -q` passed.

Reward/Smart Message idempotency evidence: `supabase/functions/_shared/idempotency.ts` can now bind an idempotency key to a request fingerprint. `grant-toss-points` fingerprints `userId`, `points`, `reasonCode`, and `idempotencyKey`; `send-smart-message` fingerprints `userId`, notification type, approved template code, variables, and `idempotencyKey`. Reusing a completed key with the same request still replays the response without another Toss call, while changing the point target, point amount, approved point reason, message target, or approved message template now returns `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` before `getPointsGrantKey` or `sendSmartMessage` can run. Smart Message now also rejects malformed non-UUID `userId` values before preference lookup, Toss user-key resolution, or message send, including service-role calls. Latest Edge regression run: `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='send-smart-message'` passed 21 suites / 161 tests, `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='grant-toss-points'` passed 21 suites / 160 tests, and the broader frontend/Supabase static gate passed 80 tests.

Point-event allowlist evidence: `process-point-events` intentionally drains only service-role calls and only allows the tuple set `referral_granted/referral_reward`, `first_coaching_created/first_coaching_bonus`, and `signup_completed/signup_bonus`; `ad_reward_callback/ad_reward` rows are now an explicit regression case that fails with `INVALID_POINT_EVENT` before any Toss grant call, and `grant-toss-points` separately rejects an `ad_reward` reason code before requesting a grant key. The drainer now also rejects otherwise allowed point events when `source_id` is missing, and migration `20260601001700_require_point_event_source_id.sql` adds a DB-level `source_id IS NOT NULL` check for new queue rows so the `(user_id,event_type,source_id)` duplicate guard cannot be bypassed with null sources. The DB trigger producers were aligned to those same tuples in migrations `20260522000500`, `20260523000100`, plus remote-corrective migration `20260601001500_align_point_event_allowlist.sql`, and `Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_point_event_producers_match_drainer_allowlist` now blocks drift back to stale `referral_success`, `first_coaching`, or raw `signup_bonus` event types. This preserves the fail-closed abuse boundary without silently failing legitimate queued bonuses.

Ad reward callback evidence: frontend rewarded-ad callbacks are now guarded by `Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_rewarded_ad_callbacks_do_not_grant_points_tokens_or_entitlements`. The only allowed effects are R1 local detail unlock (`setIsDetailUnlocked(true)`), R2 navigation to `/coaching/result`, and R3 noop/support copy. The test fails if these paths start calling `grant-toss-points`, point-event drainers, referral processors, IAP verification, coaching generation, direct Supabase subscription/order/user-entitlement writes, or AI token fields. Latest focused validation: `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py -q` passed 38 tests.

mTLS/AIT evidence: `resolveMtlsMode()` continues to allow mock mTLS only in explicit DEV_LOCAL/test contexts and returns `real` for production-like, sandbox, prod-read, prod-ready, missing, or ambiguous modes. `SANDBOX_REAL`, `PROD_READ`, and `PROD_READY` now win over conflicting dev/test signals such as `NODE_ENV=test`, so an upload-oriented runtime mode cannot be accidentally downgraded to mock by a leftover test environment value. `mTLSClient` now has a regression proving real-mode Toss network/handshake failures reject with `TOSS_UPSTREAM_NETWORK` across login token exchange, profile fetch, IAP order verification, Smart Message, and points APIs instead of returning any success payload. Full live audit now runs a local runtime hardening source scan immediately after the AIT release artifact scan and fails if production-like mTLS mode, real-mode mTLS client failures, or real-mode report AI key requirements drift out of the source. It also checks `supabase secrets list --project-ref gxvtgrcqkbdibkyeqyil --output json` for required Edge secret names `TOSS_CLIENT_CERT_BASE64`, `TOSS_CLIENT_KEY_BASE64`, `TOSS_PII_DECRYPTION_KEY_BASE64`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` without printing secret values. `TOSS_CLIENT_SECRET` is not read by the current Toss S2S/mTLS source and remains a forbidden release/log marker rather than a required Edge runtime secret. The AIT scanner still rejects `TOSS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `REPORT_AI_MODE=mock`, `sourceMappingURL=`, `MockMTLSClient`, `components/shared/DevMenu`, dev override setters, camelCase token/key literals such as `accessToken='eyJ...'`, `serviceRoleKey='...'`, `authorizationCode='...'`, and `tossUserKey='...'`; it also catches unquoted literal variants such as `serviceRoleKey=service-role-secret`, `authCode=auth-code-secret`, `tossUserKey=toss-user-key`, `email=parent@example.com`, and `phone=010-1234-5678` while avoiding normal variable/property assignments. JSON-style quoted env keys such as `"TOSS_MTLS_MODE":"mock"`, `"REPORT_AI_MODE":"mock"`, `"TOSS_RUNTIME_MODE":"DEV_LOCAL"`, and `"EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOW_DEV_MENU":"true"` are blocked, and local/private URLs now include `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, `10.0.2.2`, `192.168.*`, `172.16-31.*`, `169.254.*`, and `[::1]`. It now also checks the archive file list and blocks secret-bearing files such as `.env*`, certificate/key archives (`.pem`, `.key`, `.p12`, `.pfx`, `.crt`, `.cer`), and SSH key names even if their contents do not contain marker-shaped secrets. `strip-release-source-maps.js` recursively removes nested `.map` files and JS `sourceMappingURL` comments from both AIT archives and `dist/`. Latest focused validation also includes `node --check scripts/live-security-audit.js`, a direct `auditLocalRuntimeHardening()` helper run, and `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_live_security_audit_script_covers_supabase_blocker_requirements -q`; all passed. PII/log evidence: backend, frontend, and Edge redaction now cover snake_case, kebab-case, and camelCase token names in unstructured strings, including `authorization_code`, `authorizationCode`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `idToken`, `serviceRoleKey`, `supabaseServiceRoleKey`, `apiKey`, and `tossUserKey`. FastAPI request middleware redacts unexpected exception text before logging, and frontend backend-fallback diagnostics log only a redacted `{name,message,status,details}` shape instead of raw Error objects. The live log audit scanner now checks both exact markers and regex variants for auth codes, JWT-looking access/refresh/id tokens, bearer JWTs, opaque bearer tokens, service role/API keys, Toss user keys, private keys, emails, and KR/US phone numbers, so exported Edge logs can catch common serialization variants such as `accessToken=eyJ...`, `authorization: bearer opaque-token`, `serviceRoleKey=...`, or `tossUserKey=...`. JSON/JSONL Edge exports are also normalized before scanning, including nested arrays/objects and `{key|name,value|message}` pairs, so split fields such as `{ "key": "accessToken", "value": "eyJ..." }` still fail as `jwt-token`. Empty log exports now fail closed instead of producing a false PASS. The same scanner now also runs against public Edge, public FastAPI, authenticated RLS REST, and authenticated RLS FastAPI probe response bodies, so a 401/403/404/5xx failure response still fails the live audit if it echoes an auth code, bearer/JWT token, service key, Toss user key, email, or phone number. `--log-scan-only` lets exported logs be checked independently while Supabase management access is blocked, and full `npm run security:live-audit` now treats a missing log export as incomplete instead of skipping it. Frontend auth/route-guard evidence: AuthContext cold-start restore uses `authApi.getSession()` instead of raw `supabase.auth.getSession()`, so stored sessions are JWT-shaped and verified by `supabase.auth.getUser()` before `isAuthenticated=true`. Auth state change events are also re-verified before state is accepted. B2B route roles are resolved from `public.users.role`; forged `user_metadata.role` alone is ignored. Route guard tests now assert that `b2bOnly` pages redirect authenticated users to `/dashboard` until a verified B2B role exists, and that unauthenticated users hit `/onboarding/welcome` before any role check. Static route inventory coverage now classifies every `src/pages/**` route into explicit public/redirect, public `skipAuth`, onboarding-auth, protected-auth, or B2B-auth buckets. It verifies that dashboard, dog, settings, training, and coaching pages use `usePageGuard` with the correct `currentPath` and no `skipAuth`; onboarding continuation pages use `skipOnboarding` but still require auth; ops pages and authenticated `/parent/reports` use `requireFeature: 'b2bOnly'`; and only `/onboarding/welcome`, `/report/[shareToken]`, plus the shared-token branch inside `/parent/reports` can opt out of auth. The FastAPI frontend client also strips caller-provided `Authorization`, `apikey`, `x-user-role`, `x-user-id`, and `x-org-role` headers before fetch. Protected calls attach only a Supabase-verified JWT, while public calls drop missing, malformed, or Supabase-rejected stored tokens and continue without `Authorization`; a JWT-shaped but expired/invalid stored token is signed out and not forwarded. Latest focused validation on 2026-06-01: `npx jest src/lib/api/__tests__/backend.test.ts --runInBand --passWithNoTests` passed 1 suite / 9 tests; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_backend_client_validates_session_token_before_authorization_header -q` passed; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_route_guard_inventory_matches_expected_auth_boundaries -q` passed; `npx jest src/lib/hooks/__tests__/usePageGuard.test.ts src/lib/guards/__tests__/roleGuard.test.ts --runInBand --passWithNoTests` passed 2 suites / 21 tests. Earlier focused validation remains: `npx jest src/lib/api/__tests__/auth.test.ts src/stores/__tests__/AuthContext.test.ts --runInBand --passWithNoTests` passed 2 suites / 25 tests; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py Backend/tests/test_security.py -q` passed 59 tests; latest `npm run security:live-audit` passed all public Edge spoof probes plus all protected backend probes before exiting non-zero for the remaining secret/log/RLS fixture blockers.

Toss Login bridge-token evidence: `login-with-toss` now rejects a malformed Supabase bridge `accessToken` before returning a session payload, so the server boundary also fails closed if the internal bridge emits a non-JWT access token. The existing client-side `setSessionFromBridgeResponse()` and `authApi.getSession()` checks still verify JWT shape with `supabase.auth.getUser()`, and the Edge handler now mirrors that first shape gate before response. Auth-code replay detection is also referrer-independent: once a code is consumed after a successful Toss exchange, replaying the same code with a different `referrer` returns `AUTH_CODE_REUSED` before another Toss/mTLS exchange or Supabase bridge attempt. Latest focused validation on 2026-06-01: `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='login-with-toss'` passed 21 suites / 149 tests, `npx jest src/lib/api/__tests__/auth.test.ts src/stores/__tests__/AuthContext.test.ts --runInBand --passWithNoTests` passed 2 suites / 25 tests, `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_security.py -q` passed 21 tests, and the broader frontend/Supabase security static gate passed 79 tests.

`verify_jwt=false` internal-auth evidence: static guards now require every protected `verify_jwt=false` function to do more than merely contain `/auth/v1/user`. For `assign-b2b-role` and `withdraw-user`, the guard verifies that the request `Authorization` header must be a bearer token, that the exact token is checked through `/auth/v1/user`, that no `x-user-role` header is read, and that privileged writes are bound to the verified owner id. `assign-b2b-role` must not read `body.userId`; `withdraw-user` may accept `body.userId` only after comparing it to `verified.userId`. For `verify-iap-order`, the guard verifies the request bearer token is either the exact trusted service-role key or is checked by `verifyJwtViaAuth(token)`, and that body `userId` is resolved together with the authenticated user id instead of trusted directly. Role-protected gateway-JWT functions (`grant-toss-points`, `send-smart-message`, `generate-report`) are also statically required to build their Edge context through `buildEdgeContext(request)` and not read `x-user-role` from request headers. Full live audit repeats a local Edge function config/source auth scan and then verifies live `verify_jwt` settings through Supabase management. It checks local expectations for `login-with-toss`, `verify-iap-order`, `grant-toss-points`, `send-smart-message`, `generate-report`, `assign-b2b-role`, and `withdraw-user`; verifies entrypoints exist; rejects protected internal-auth source drift away from `/auth/v1/user`; rejects spoofable `x-user-role` reads; and ensures `login-with-toss` consumes the authCode before profile fetch or Supabase bridge session creation. The shared HTTP adapter now has a regression proving a spoofed `x-user-role: service_role` header cannot override a lower-privilege JWT claim. The live FastAPI backend probe now includes the IAP proxy mutation endpoint and confirms missing, malformed, expired-test JWT, and `x-user-role: trainer` spoof requests all return 401 before the proxy can forward to Edge. Latest focused validation on 2026-06-01: `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='httpAdapter|edge-config-security'` passed 21 suites / 147 tests; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_edge_context_does_not_trust_user_metadata_for_roles Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_role_protected_edge_entrypoints_use_jwt_context_not_role_headers -q` passed 2 tests; `npm run security:live-audit -- --backend-probes-only` passed protected read and mutation probes. Earlier `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='edge-config-security|assign-b2b-role|withdraw-user|verify-iap-order-auth'` passed 21 suites / 141 tests, and `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py -q` passed 36 tests. Full `npm run security:live-audit` now proves live function auth settings before exiting non-zero for the remaining secret/log/RLS fixture blockers.

IAP proxy-specific evidence: `Backend/tests/test_subscription_security.py::test_iap_proxy_endpoint_forwards_authenticated_user_id_not_body_user_id` invokes the FastAPI proxy endpoint with an attacker-supplied `body.userId` and verifies the forwarded Edge Function JSON uses the authenticated backend user id plus the configured service role key. The proxy also rejects B2C product ids that include `orgId` or `trainerUserId`, so a caller cannot smuggle B2B scope fields into a personal subscription purchase before the service-role forward. This pairs with Edge tests proving direct non-service callers ignore `body.userId`, service-role callers require a UUID `userId`, idempotency replays are bound to the original user/product/order/scope, and `grant_status=granted` is only persisted after subscription or org-subscription activation succeeds. Latest focused validation: `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_subscription_security.py -q` passed 13 tests, and `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_b2b_iap_scope_is_server_verified_and_idempotency_bound -q` passed.

IAP order-reuse evidence: `verify-iap-order` now checks existing `toss_orders` by both `idempotency_key` and `toss_order_id` before any mTLS verification, subscription activation, token increment, or org-subscription activation can run. A replay of the same Toss order id with a different idempotency key returns `IAP_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` instead of creating a second grant path. Exact replays of an existing `grant_status=granted` row now also re-check the entitlement ledger before returning success: B2C plan products require an active matching `subscriptions` row, token products require a subscription ledger with at least the granted token total, and B2B products require an active/trial `org_subscriptions` row bound to the same Toss order id. If that ledger is missing, replay fails closed with `IAP_GRANT_LEDGER_INCONSISTENT` instead of treating an orphaned granted order as a valid entitlement. Migration `20260601001600_lock_toss_order_id_reuse.sql` adds a partial unique index on `toss_order_id` as the DB-level ledger invariant. The grant finalization step also fails closed when Toss reports a paid order but the entitlement write does not complete: B2C subscription writes, B2C token increments, and B2B org/trainer subscription writes all persist `grant_status=grant_failed` instead of a granted ledger row with no matching entitlement. Unknown paid product ids also persist `grant_failed` with `IAP_PRODUCT_GRANT_UNKNOWN`. Latest focused validation on 2026-06-01: `npm run test:edge -- --testPathPattern='verify-iap-order-auth'` passed 21 suites / 151 tests; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_verify_iap_order_idempotency_is_bound_before_grant Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_verify_iap_order_only_marks_granted_after_subscription_activation -q` passed 2 tests; the broader frontend/Supabase static gate passed 79 tests; `deno check supabase/functions/verify-iap-order/main.ts` is blocked by the repo `tsconfig.json` value `jsx=react-native`, which Deno does not support.

B2B assignment evidence: `verify_dog_ownership` now accepts an organization assignment only when the assignment's `org_id` still has an active `org_dogs` row for the same dog. `Backend/tests/test_ownership.py::test_verify_dog_ownership_rejects_stale_org_assignment_when_org_dog_is_inactive` prevents a stale active assignment row from preserving access after the dog leaves the organization, while the personal assignment path remains unchanged.

Dog profile/env write evidence: `Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py::test_dogs_and_dog_env_writes_are_owner_bound` now proves the DB policies for `dogs` and `dog_env` update/delete are tied to `auth.uid()` ownership, and that FastAPI `update_dog_profile`/`delete_dog` call `verify_dog_ownership` before mutating `Dog` or deleting it. It also verifies the frontend dog API goes through `/api/v1/dogs/*` and does not directly access Supabase `dogs` or `dog_env` tables. Latest focused validation: `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py -q` passed 38 tests.

RLS route-boundary evidence: org-scoped collection routes now have a static guard proving each list/count/stat endpoint verifies `service.verify_org_membership(db, org_id, user_id)` before calling the underlying data-access service. This covers members, member counts, org dogs, dog counts, org assignments, and today's org stats, preventing a future router edit from exposing broad org collections before the B2B membership boundary. The live audit helper now also has authenticated RLS cross-access probes for Supabase REST read probes, Supabase REST update probes, forged insert probes, FastAPI resource reads, and FastAPI mutation routes, so future QA can prove that an attacker JWT cannot read, update, or forge another user's dog, coaching-result (`ai_coaching`), recommendation, training, settings, entitlement, media, subscription, order, organization, org subscription, or report rows without Supabase management API access. Full `npm run security:live-audit` now runs a local RLS policy source scan before authenticated fixture probes: it requires RLS enablement for every table in the live RLS probe set; rejects direct public/authenticated policies on service-role-only AI/media tables; confirms latest `subscriptions` and `toss_orders` lock migrations do not reintroduce public writes; and checks the stricter `org_dogs` and `daily_reports` owner/member/trainer scoping markers. Full audit then runs the authenticated probes automatically and fails closed without attacker JWT/fixture inputs; complete RLS mode requires all cross-user fixture ids plus `--rls-victim-user-id` by default, and the helper decodes the attacker JWT before live calls. It now rejects attacker JWTs with non-UUID `sub`, missing/expired `exp`, or `anon`/`service_role` roles because those fixtures cannot prove ordinary user-level RLS isolation; it also fails if the attacker `sub` matches either `--rls-victim-user-id` or `--rls-subscription-user-id`. `--rls-fixture-file` loads the same values from a local JSON file so bearer tokens can stay out of shell history and process listings; `.gitignore` blocks `security-rls-fixture*.json` and `.security-rls-fixture*.json`. `--rls-allow-partial` is available only for intentionally scoped diagnostics. The backend mutation set covers `PUT /api/v1/dogs/{dog_id}`, `POST /api/v1/logs/quick`, `POST /api/v1/coaching/generation-jobs`, `POST /api/v1/training/status`, `PATCH /api/v1/org/{org_id}`, `POST /api/v1/org/members/invite`, `POST /api/v1/org/dogs/enroll`, `POST /api/v1/org/assignments`, `POST /api/v1/report/`, `PATCH /api/v1/report/{report_id}`, and `PATCH /api/v1/report/{report_id}/send`; any 2xx response to the attacker JWT is treated as a leak. Latest focused validation on 2026-06-01: `node --check scripts/live-security-audit.js` passed; a direct Node helper check proved fixture files load attacker/victim/resource ids, CLI args override file values, unknown fixture fields are rejected, same-user RLS fixtures are rejected, attacker JWT fixtures with `anon` role, `service_role` role, expired `exp`, or non-UUID `sub` are rejected, `--rls-victim-user-id` is required for complete mode, forged insert/backend mutation probes use the victim user id instead of the attacker or ledger fallback id, and `auditLocalRlsPolicySource()` passes for 23 RLS probe tables; `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=dummy npm run security:live-audit -- --rls-probes-only --rls-fixture-file <same-user-fixture> --rls-allow-partial` failed closed with `RLS attacker JWT subject matches --rls-victim-user-id`; `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_live_security_audit_script_covers_supabase_blocker_requirements -q` passed; and the broader `Backend/venv/bin/pytest Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py Backend/tests/test_supabase_security_static.py -q` passed 79 tests. Full `npm run security:live-audit` still fails because live management, log export, and authenticated RLS fixtures are not available.

After Supabase project privileges are fixed, verify:

1. `verify_jwt=false` functions still perform internal JWT/service-role checks.
2. Deployed Edge source matches local hardened files.
3. Required Edge secret names for real mTLS, PII, and report AI are present.
4. Live logs contain no raw tokens, API keys, service role keys, auth codes, phone numbers, or emails.
5. RLS policies for orders, subscriptions, org dogs, and daily reports match the new migrations.
6. Production-like Edge environment uses real mTLS mode and does not expose mock mode.
7. The AIT upload artifact is built through `scripts/build-ait-release.js` and scanned before upload.

Read-only helper:

```bash
npm run security:live-audit
npm run security:live-audit -- --log-file <edge-log-export.txt> --require-log-file
npm run security:live-audit -- --log-scan-only --log-file <edge-log-export.txt>
npm run security:live-audit -- --edge-probes-only
npm run security:live-audit -- --backend-probes-only

npm run security:live-audit -- --rls-probes-only --rls-attacker-jwt <jwt> --rls-victim-user-id <other-user-id> --rls-dog-id <other-user-dog-id>
```

The helper defaults to the current TaillogToss Supabase project ref `gxvtgrcqkbdibkyeqyil` so stale shell environment values cannot point the audit at an old project. It runs the AIT upload artifact scanner against the current `taillog-app.ait`; checks live Edge `verify_jwt` settings for `verify-iap-order`, `grant-toss-points`, `send-smart-message`, `generate-report`, `assign-b2b-role`, and `withdraw-user`; confirms the security migrations are present in the linked project; checks required Edge secret names for real mTLS/PII/report AI without reading values; scans an exported Edge log file for exact token/PII markers plus regex variants of auth codes, JWTs, service/API keys, Toss user keys, private keys, email addresses, and phone numbers; runs invalid auth-code probes against `login-with-toss`; runs anonymous, malformed-JWT, and expired-test-JWT baseline vs `x-user-role: trainer` spoof probes against `verify-iap-order`, `grant-toss-points`, `send-smart-message`, and `generate-report`; scans those probe response bodies for sensitive echo leaks; verifies public FastAPI protected read and mutation endpoints return 401 for missing, malformed, and expired-test bearer tokens with or without a spoofed role header; scans those backend error bodies for the same leaks; and runs authenticated cross-user RLS probes when given a real attacker JWT and target resource ids. Prefer `--rls-fixture-file` for RLS runs so bearer tokens stay out of shell history/process listings; `security-rls-fixture*.json` and `.security-rls-fixture*.json` are gitignored. Use `--log-scan-only` when only exported logs are available and Supabase management access is still blocked. In full mode it continues to public probes even if artifact/management/log/RLS checks are blocked, then exits non-zero with `security live audit incomplete` until the upload artifact passes, Supabase project privileges, linked migration access, required Edge secret names, exported logs, and RLS fixtures are available.

## Release Build Guardrail

`npm run build` now uses `scripts/build-ait-release.js`, which:

1. passes only public AIT runtime variables from `.env`;
2. forces `NODE_ENV=production` and clears `EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOW_DEV_MENU`;
3. strips release source maps;
4. fails the build if `taillog-app.ait` still contains forbidden secret/dev/local markers or source maps;
5. re-scans the deployment-id-named copy before it can be reported for upload.

`npm run release:preflight` combines TypeScript typecheck and artifact scanning for upload readiness. `npm run release:security-check` can also be run independently before upload. By default it scans the current `taillog-app.ait`; pass explicit `.ait` paths to scan a versioned upload candidate. The scanner checks both exact markers and regex variants for mock mTLS/runtime/report-AI modes, dev menu or dev override symbols, source-map comments, local backend URLs, JWT/token-looking values, auth-code/user-key/service-role-key literals, private keys, and Toss test ad IDs. It also rejects secret-bearing archive file names such as `.env.production`, `certs/toss-client.p12`, and `keys/id_ed25519`. `Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_release_security_check_rejects_pattern_variants` creates a throwaway `.ait` with `TOSS_MTLS_MODE: 'mock'`, `REPORT_AI_MODE: 'mock'`, DevMenu override symbols, `sourceMappingURL`, `http://127.0.0.1`, `Bearer eyJ...`, `accessToken='eyJ...'`, `serviceRoleKey='...'`, `authorizationCode='...'`, `tossUserKey='...'`, keyed email, and keyed phone values to prove those variants fail the gate. `Backend/tests/test_frontend_security_static.py::test_release_security_check_rejects_secret_bearing_files` proves marker-free secret files fail by filename alone.

`.github/workflows/security-preflight.yml` runs TypeScript, release/live-audit script syntax checks, frontend/AIT static security tests, Supabase Edge/RLS static security tests, backend security regression tests, and Edge security tests on PR/push/manual runs. The backend gate covers session auth, PII log redaction, B2B scoping, report access, referral rewards, subscriptions, and dashboard dog ownership. Because `.ait` artifacts are gitignored, CI runs `npm run release:security-check` when `taillog-app.ait` is present and otherwise records that the local `npm run build` path enforces the artifact scan before upload.
